adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic existence check (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and then creates (`TopicEmbed.create!`) when blank. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so concurrent importers for the same URL can both see no row and then one `create!` will raise (e.g., unique constraint / RecordNotUnique). There is no rescue around that in the diff, so it can crash the PollFeed job / retrieve path. The finding’s claim about leaving orphaned Topic/Post is less certain because the `Topic.transaction` should roll back, but the race-to-exception itself is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40-43 — `perform_retrieve` synchronously instantiates and executes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline on the web/job-processing request path, fetching and parsing the entire remote RSS/Atom feed just to resolve one embed_url, coupling the latency and failure mode of an external feed fetch to every uncached embed request.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` does call `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items, so this can synchronously fetch/parse the entire remote feed on the embed retrieval path (which is triggered from EmbedController when no embed exists, and also from the RetrieveTopic job). This is a latency/failure-mode coupling and architectural/performance concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-33 and app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — the Redis `retrieved_recently?` throttle key is keyed per embed_url with `setnx`, but `perform_retrieve` re-checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` only after acquiring the throttle lock in a separate process, so two TopicRetriever calls that race before either sets the Redis key both pass `retrieved_recently?` as false and both proceed to `perform_retrieve`, hitting the same TOCTOU window as above.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")`, which is an atomic operation: only one concurrent caller can succeed and return `false` (allowing retrieval), while the other will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (throttled). Therefore the described scenario where “two calls both pass `retrieved_recently?` as false before either sets the Redis key” is not supported by the diff. `perform_retrieve` does re-check `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, but the finding’s claimed Redis TOCTOU window is based on a misread of the `setnx` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 and lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — `ensure_embeddable`'s referer-host check and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`'s embed_url-host check independently reimplement the same "host equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host" comparison in two files with no shared helper, so a future change to embeddable-host matching semantics (e.g. adding scheme/port/subdomain support) risks being applied to only one call site, silently reopening the bypass the other was meant to close.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate host-validation implementations: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable compares `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), while TopicRetriever#invalid_host? compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` interpolates the raw, attacker-controlled Referer header unescaped into a single-quoted JS string inside a <script> tag with no `j`/`escape_javascript`, so a Referer containing a single quote and script content (e.g. `x');alert(document.cookie);//`) breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JS in the embed frame's origin, which also has access to postMessage/topic data; confidence 95, severity P0.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` performs a substring containment check instead of exact-match/startsWith validation, so any origin string that merely contains discourseUrl as a substring (e.g. an attacker page whose origin happens to embed the discourseUrl text, or a scheme/host crafted to contain it) passes the check and can spoof discourse-resize postMessages to control the iframe height/DOM; confidence 90, severity P2.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the message-origin gate is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which accepts any `e.origin` that is a substring/prefix of `discourseUrl` rather than requiring exact origin match. Since `postMessage` can be sent from any window, an attacker-controlled iframe with an origin like `https://example.co` could pass when `discourseUrl` is `https://example.com/` (prefix match) and spoof `discourse-resize` messages to control `iframe.height`. The finding’s directionality is slightly misstated (it’s origin-in-discourseUrl, not discourseUrl-in-origin), but the underlying validation flaw is real and diff-grounded.
